title: The ad says negotiable
hook: Would stating a negotiation rule change who opens a negotiation?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Contrast ambiguity about negotiability with an explicit common rule.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Contrast ambiguity about negotiability with an explicit common rule.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy applicant believes negotiation is allowed with probability 0.3. It yields €20 if allowed and costs €4 effort. What is expected net value? Toy inputs A=[0.3, 20, 4]; B=[1, 20, 4].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[2, 0.3, 4], [16, 1, 4]]. Labels: Expected net €, Belief P, Effort €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Ambiguity changes the belief input while the skill, gain and effort cost remain fixed. The explicit-rule comparison removes that uncertainty. The toy does not attribute any observed group difference to inherent negotiating ability.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses P(allowed)=1, Gain if allowed €=20, Effort €=4. What is Expected net €? Answer: 16.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses P(allowed)=1, Gain if allowed €=20, Effort €=4. What is Expected net €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 16. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: When job ads stated wages were negotiable, the gender gap in negotiating disappeared (Leibbrandt & List, 2015).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Contrast ambiguity about negotiability with an explicit common rule.
